**Performance: PASS** at `59a35cdc15271eeffc5dab63c5178c53ec108ebd`, round 2 (final under C34).

**P220-N001's tmux-launch qualification is resolved.** Close now uses `pane_process_without_launch`, whose implementation calls only `query_live`; its default declines rather than falling back. Cold/disabled/unavailable control clients produce an unchecked pane, with no start/restart/fork. The real-tmux regression positively warms the client, then verifies existing and missing targets without an added launch, and separately checks cold/disabled cases.

An existing target normally costs one live IPC read. A failed read or empty/malformed fields can add **one live pane-list read**, O(panes), to distinguish Gone from Unchecked; that path also cannot launch. Thus one method invocation is not always one IPC operation. The shared parser fix preserves the no-launch boundary.

The other-holder veto and closed seat rendering reuse the existing registry snapshot; they add no second registry read. The common `may_close` predicate now also runs at a held close's continuation: self/parent checks remain immediate, while a dead-parentless prime case repeats the existing liveness/project-designation check there. Its O(projects) read/schema guard and the close-note's O(registry rows) work retain the prior per-operation budget, not a new tick. Existing liveness fallback behavior is not a claim of zero syscalls or all-process cost.

No new periodic loop, timer or launch site; **`spawn_sites.rs` unchanged**.
